title: Settings card: 2024 Yamaha YZ250
ig_caption:
2024 Yamaha YZ250. About 170 lb, comfortable pace, hardpack moto, stock suspension, stability and comfort the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the standard settings from the 2024 YZ250 owner's service manual.

Stock is 9 and 14 on the fork, 9 clicks and 1 1/8 turns on the shock, 8 on shock rebound, and Yamaha's 90 to 100 mm sag window. Dialed moved one thing: shock high-speed a quarter turn out, to 1 3/8. Sag at 100. For this rider on hardpack, stock is already close, so the first move is a small one.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

title: Settings card: 2026 Kawasaki KX250
ig_caption:
2026 Kawasaki KX250. About 135 lb, fast, supercross style track, stock suspension, stability and jump support the goals. Left is stock from the 2026 KX250 owner's manual, right is the baseline Dialed built for that rider.

Fork comp 8 to 7, fork rebound 7 to 8. Shock low-speed stays at 11, high-speed stays at 2 1/2 turns, rebound 10 to 11. Sag set at 103 mm; check your manual for Kawasaki's figure. Small moves: one click in on fork comp for jump faces, and a quicker return front and rear for a light rider.

title: Carousel: rebound, the clicker riders forget
ig_caption:
Riders spend weeks on compression and never touch rebound. Rebound doesn't change how hard the fork or shock hits. It changes how fast it comes back after.

Too fast and the bike feels light and kicks. Too slow and it packs down. One click at a time, counted out from fully closed.

title: Settings card: 2020 KTM 300 XC
ig_caption:
2020 KTM 300 XC. About 175 lb, intermediate, roots and hardpack, short motos, stability and comfort the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the standard settings from KTM's 2020 owner's manual for the 250 and 300 XC TPI (US edition).

Stock is 12 and 12 on the fork, 15 clicks and 2 turns on the shock, 15 on shock rebound, 105 mm of riding sag. Dialed went 2 clicks out on fork comp, 3 in on low-speed, a full turn in on high-speed and 1 in on shock rebound. Fork rebound and sag stay stock. A softer front for the roots, more hold out back for the ledges and hardpack hits.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

title: Settings card: 2024 KTM 250 SX
ig_caption:
2024 KTM 250 SX. About 165 lb, pro pace, sand moto, stability and jump support the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the standard settings from KTM's 2024 owner's manual for the 250 SX, 300 SX, 250 XC and 300 XC.

Stock is 12 and 18 on the fork, 15 clicks and 1 1/2 turns on the shock, 15 on shock rebound, 105 mm of riding sag. Dialed went 1 click out on fork comp, 7 in on fork rebound, 5 in on low-speed and 1 in on shock rebound. High-speed and sag stay stock. Seven clicks is a big move: if the front starts to feel slow or packs in the whoops, come back toward stock two at a time. Fork air: set it from the manual for your weight.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

title: Comment answer: soft lows, firm highs
ig_caption:
A comment on our CRF250R card picked up on it: the low-speed went softer while the high-speed went firmer. That isn't a contradiction. The two adjusters on the shock do different jobs.

Low-speed handles the slow stuff, like squat on the gas. High-speed handles the fast hits, like landings and square edges. Starting points, refined on the bike one change at a time, counted out from fully closed.
